data.gender_notes: Munaqqaa is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Munaqqaa means a resting place, shelter, refuge, or a place of safety. It is derived from the Arabic verb nakaha, which means to take refuge or seek shelter. The name Munaqqaa carries the meaning “Resting place, refuge” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Munaqqaa usually hope their child will grow to embody resting place, refuge and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Munaqqaa total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Munaqqaa is deeply rooted in both the Islamic religious and cultural contexts. One of the important practices in Islam is the annual pilgrimage, Hajj. During this journey, every pilgrim visits the holy city of Mecca and circles the Kaaba seven times, which is called Tawaf. The Kaaba, as the holiest site in Islam, represents a collective refuge and a symbol of unity for all Muslims around the world. The name Munaqqaa in this context can be seen as a reminder of the spiritual sanctity and refuge that the Kaaba provides for every Muslim during their pilgrimage.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, Munaqqaa signifies seeking refuge and protection in Allah. It is a reminder of the belief in the Quran that "And with Allah is the refuge" (Kindah 115). Muslims strive to seek His protection and guidance throughout their lives and turn towards Him in times of need, seeking His refuge and mercy. The name Munaqqaa, therefore, serves as a call to remember Allah's endless love, mercy, and protection, and to constantly seek His shelter and refuge in all aspects of life.
